titulo: Müssen, wollen and dürfen: obligation, wish and permission: Müssen: have to

aula.titulo: Müssen, wollen and dürfen: obligation, wish and permission
aula.objetivo: Use «müssen» (have to), «wollen» (want to) and «dürfen» (be allowed to), and read the most common signs — always with the sentence bracket.

blocos.titulo: Müssen: obligation and necessity, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: «müssen» expresses what you HAVE TO do (obligation or necessity): «Ich muss arbeiten» = I have to work / I must work — "must" is its English cousin. STEP 2: conjugate: ich muss, du musst, er muss, wir müssen, ihr müsst, sie müssen. The «ü» disappears in the singular and, as with «können», «ich» and «er» are the same, with no -t. STEP 3: the second verb goes to the END, in the infinitive: «Du musst pünktlich sein.» STEP 4: question: «Muss ich heute arbeiten?» STEP 5: a separable verb stays WHOLE at the end: «Ich muss um sieben Uhr aufstehen.» English needs "have to" (two words plus "to"); German has one modal and no "to".
blocos.comparacao: English says "I have to work" or "I must work". German only has the second pattern: «Ich muss arbeiten», with the infinitive at the end of the sentence. And remember the trap from lesson 11: «Ich muss nicht» means "I don't have to", not "I mustn't".

erros.errado: Ich muss aufstehe um sieben Uhr.
erros.certo: Ich muss um sieben Uhr aufstehen.
erros.motivo: The whole infinitive goes to the end.

blocos.enunciado: Say 5 things you have to do today: «Ich muss …»
Write the 6 forms of «können» and one sentence with each.
